### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Electron Version

39.2.7

### What operating system(s) are you using?

Other Linux

### Operating System Version

Linux lubuntu-rm78-standardpc 6.17.0-20-generic #20~24.04.1-Ubuntu SMP PREEMPT_DYNAMIC Thu Mar 19 01:28:37 UTC 2 x86_64 x86_64 x86_64 GNU/Linux

### What arch are you using?

x64

### Last Known Working Electron version

_No response_

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

I don't know how to test

### Expected Behavior

If restart is requested, Electron needs to start the app the same way it started the first time.

In this case that means:

- the current process shuts down
- the replacement process starts
- the new process reaches the app's entrypoint again
- the lifecycle trace shows a second `process-start`

Something like this:

```
pid=old restart-requested
pid=old app-relaunch-scheduled
pid=old before-quit:app-exit
pid=new process-start
pid=new single-instance-lock-acquired
```

### Actual Behavior

On my Lubuntu VM, the original process behaves exactly as if restart is happening, but the replacement process never appears. Restart worked normally until I switched `sandbox` to `true`

The trace shows:

```text
pid=4895 restart-requested
pid=4895 app-relaunch-scheduled {"reason":"restart-request","execPath":"/home/lubuntu-rm78/programming/Kiyeovo/node_modules/electron/dist/electron","args":["/home/lubuntu-rm78/programming/Kiyeovo"],"cwd":"/home/lubuntu-rm78/programming/Kiyeovo"}
pid=4895 before-quit {"hasP2PCore":false,"hasTorManager":true,"restartRequested":true}
pid=4895 app-relaunch-already-scheduled {"reason":"before-quit-with-cleanup-fallback"}
pid=4895 before-quit:app-exit {"exitCode":0}
pid=4895 main-window:closed
```

and then nothing after that. There is no second `process-start`, so the restarted instance never gets far enough to enter the app's startup code.

The app uses `app.requestSingleInstanceLock()`. If the new process had started and lost the lock, I would still expect a second `process-start`, but there was no second startup at all.

I also tried scheduling relaunch earlier at restart request time instead of only during `before-quit`. No difference.

### Workaround That Fixes It

I replaced `app.relaunch()` with spawn:

```ts
const child = spawn(process.execPath, [absoluteAppPath], {
  cwd: process.cwd(),
  detached: true,
  env: process.env,
  stdio: 'ignore',
});
child.unref();
app.exit(0);
```

After that, the log becomes:

```text
pid=5203 restart-requested
pid=5203 app-relaunch-scheduled {"mode":"spawn-detached", ...}
pid=5203 app-relaunch-spawned {"childPid":5314, ...}
pid=5203 before-quit:app-exit-no-cleanup {"exitCode":0}
pid=5314 process-start
pid=5314 single-instance-lock-acquired
...
```

So the same app on the same machine and same sandbox settings works as soon as the relaunch is done via the spawn call.

It is also worth nothing that it works on my local machine, but it does not on my Lubuntu VM.
Local machine: `Linux rm78-workstation 6.1.0-44-amd64 #1 SMP PREEMPT_DYNAMIC Debian 6.1.164-1 (2026-03-09) x86_64 GNU/Linux`
Lubuntu VM: `Linux lubuntu-rm78-standardpc 6.17.0-20-generic #20~24.04.1-Ubuntu SMP PREEMPT_DYNAMIC Thu Mar 19 01:28:37 UTC 2 x86_64 x86_64 x86_64 GNU/Linux`

### Testcase Gist URL

_No response_

### Additional Information

You can find the app that I'm talking about here: https://github.com/Realman78/Kiyeovo/tree/security-hardening

nodes.title: DCHECK in weak_ptr.h during ~WebContents() when 'blur' is emitted via ~InspectableWebContents on macOS
nodes.body:
### Scope

**DCHECK-only** — fires in testing/debug builds (`DCHECK_IS_ON()`); release builds are unaffected at the crash site, though the underlying re-entrancy is still present.

### Summary

On macOS, `electron::api::WebContents::~WebContents()` can re-enter JS via the focus-loss observer callback **after** `weak_factory_` has already been destructed, tripping `DCHECK(ptr)` at `base/memory/weak_ptr.h:298`.

### Stack

```
WebContents::Destroy()                               <- GetWeakPtr() DCHECKs (ptr_ == 0)
gin_helper::Dispatcher<void(WebContents*)>::DispatchToCallback
...V8 microtask...
v8::internal::MicrotaskQueue::PerformCheckpointInternal
node::InternalCallbackScope::Close()
gin_helper::internal::CallMethodWithArgs             <- Emit("blur")
EventEmitterMixin<WebContents>::Emit
WebContentsImpl::NotifyWebContentsLostFocus
RenderWidgetHostImpl::LostFocus
RenderWidgetHostViewMac::SetActive(false)
-[RenderWidgetHostViewCocoa viewDidMoveToWindow]
-[NSView removeFromSuperview]
WebContentsViewMac::ViewsHostableDetach
views::NativeViewHostMac::NativeViewDetaching
views::WebView::SetWebContents(nullptr)
InspectableWebContentsView::~InspectableWebContentsView
InspectableWebContents::~InspectableWebContents       <- member dtor (after ~weak_factory_)
api::WebContents::~WebContents
api::WebContents::DeleteThisIfAlive
```

### Sequence

1. `~WebContents()` body runs.
2. Members destroy in reverse declaration order: `weak_factory_` is last-declared so its dtor runs **first** (`ptr_ = 0`), then `~inspectable_web_contents_`.
3. `~InspectableWebContents` detaches the native view → AppKit `removeFromSuperview` → `viewDidMoveToWindow` → `SetActive(false)` → `LostFocus` chain.
4. `OnWebContentsLostFocus` → `Emit("blur")` on the WebContents that is mid-destruction.
5. `~node::CallbackScope` runs a microtask checkpoint; a pending microtask (e.g. the continuation of an `await once(wc, ...)`) runs.
6. That JS calls `.destroy()` (or another method that hits `GetWeakPtr()`) → `weak_factory_.GetWeakPtr()` constructs `WeakPtr(ref, 0)` → DCHECK.

### Repro

`spec/api-web-contents-view.spec.ts` test **`does not crash when closed via window.close()`** (currently `it.skip`'d on the vitest migration branch with a TODO pointing here). Its `wc.on('blur', ...)` handler is the re-entry vector.

### Prior art for a fix

- `BaseWindow::OnWindowClosed()` (`electron_api_base_window.cc`) does `weak_factory_.InvalidateWeakPtrs()` + `MarkDestroyed()` before emitting, with a comment explaining the same concern.
- `content::WebContentsImpl::~WebContentsImpl()` sets `is_being_destroyed_ = true` first thing.

A verified fix is adding an `is_being_destroyed_` flag set at the top of `~WebContents()` and guarding `OnWebContentsFocused` / `OnWebContentsLostFocus` with it. That stops the DCHECK, but it's a behaviour change — `'blur'` no longer fires during WebContents destruction — which invalidates the premise of the #47933 test. Needs a decision on whether suppressing the event is acceptable, or whether a narrower fix (e.g. resetting `inspectable_web_contents_` explicitly at the end of the dtor body so view-detach runs while `weak_factory_` is still valid) is preferable.

nodes.title: [Bug]: autoUpdater silently fails on macOS — ShipIt launchd job pends on unsatisfiable SuccessfulExit semaphore
nodes.body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Electron Version

37.6.0 (bundled in Discord 0.0.383 — see Additional Information for why I'm filing downstream)

### What operating system(s) are you using?

macOS

### Operating System Version

Darwin 25.3.0

### What arch are you using?

arm64 (including Apple Silicon)

### Last Known Working Electron version

Unknown. Prior updates on the same machine completed successfully through 2026-03-10 per `ShipIt_stderr.log`; the failure is latent and only surfaces once the ShipIt LaunchAgent gets `launchctl disable`d at some point and is then recovered.

### Expected Behavior

After `autoUpdater.quitAndInstall()`, the main process exits, ShipIt runs, the staged update is installed, and the app relaunches.

### Actual Behavior

Main process exits cleanly. ShipIt never spawns. `ShipIt_stderr.log` receives zero new lines across multiple update attempts. No error surfaced to the app, the user, or the unified log. Manual `launchctl kickstart` is the only recovery.

### Testcase Gist URL

_No response_

### Additional Information

Although the observed failure came from Discord’s Electron 37.6.0, I do not believe this is specific to 37.x. Electron’s vendored Squirrel.Mac patch at `patches/squirrel.mac/build_add_gn_config.patch` is identical across the current `38-x-y`, `39-x-y`, `40-x-y`, and `41-x-y` branches, and the suspected failure is in the ShipIt launcher / `SMJobSubmit` path rather than downstream app code. In other words, the report was discovered on 37.6.0, but the code path appears shared by supported Electron lines as well.

Hit this chasing a Discord update that silently refused to apply. Discord ships Electron 37.6.0, so filing here rather than in Discord's support portal where it'll just get "please reinstall"ed — and reinstalling provably doesn't fix it because the bad state lives in launchd, not in the `.app` bundle.

Same bug as Squirrel/Squirrel.Mac#196 (filed 2017, still open, zero replies in 9 years) with an almost-fix in Squirrel/Squirrel.Mac#197 (closed unmerged). I left the full writeup with the actual launchctl state dump on the #196 thread, linking here for anyone who wants to skip ahead: https://github.com/Squirrel/Squirrel.Mac/issues/196#issuecomment-4219698997

Short version: after `SMJobSubmit` the ShipIt job is registered fine and `RunAtLoad` is set, but launchd pends the initial spawn on an unsatisfiable `successful exit` semaphore and the job never executes. `launchctl print gui/$(id -u)/com.hnc.Discord.ShipIt`:

    runs = 0
    pended nondemand spawn = semaphore
    semaphores = {
        successful exit => 0
    }

I think what's happening is that the `KeepAlive = { SuccessfulExit = NO; }` clause in `Squirrel/SQRLShipItLauncher.m` is being evaluated by launchd as a precondition for the *initial* spawn, not just for keepalive restarts. On older macOS the keepalive dict only kicked in after `runs >= 1`, so `RunAtLoad` always fired cleanly. On Darwin 25 (possibly earlier, haven't bisected) launchd is checking the clause before the first spawn, and since "previous run exited non-successfully" can never be true when `runs = 0`, the spawn pends indefinitely. `launchctl kickstart` bypasses the semaphore and ShipIt runs to completion immediately, which tells me the job itself is fine — it's the spawn gating that's broken.

There's a secondary condition needed for this to manifest organically: the affected user's `com.hnc.Discord.ShipIt`, `com.microsoft.VSCode.ShipIt`, and `com.anthropic.claudefordesktop.ShipIt` were all in the launchd disabled override list (`launchctl print-disabled gui/$(id -u)` reported `=> disabled` for all three). User has no memory of running `launchctl disable` — some hardening/privacy tool presumably did. Clearing the override with `launchctl enable` is necessary but not sufficient; the pended-semaphore state still blocks the first spawn after re-enable, and that's the half I think is actually a Squirrel/Electron concern, since it silently wedges any affected user permanently and there's nothing in the autoUpdater API that surfaces it.

This can be reproduced on any Electron app using `autoUpdater` without waiting for an organic disable — just induce the state manually:

    # pick any Electron app using autoUpdater
    launchctl disable gui/$(id -u)/<app-bundle-id>.ShipIt
    # trigger an update inside the app so SMJobSubmit gets called
    # (the update will silently fail to apply)
    launchctl enable gui/$(id -u)/<app-bundle-id>.ShipIt
    # inspect the submitted job
    launchctl print gui/$(id -u)/<app-bundle-id>.ShipIt

`runs = 0` and `pended nondemand spawn = semaphore` should both be visible, and the job will never spawn on its own from that state no matter how long you wait or how many times the app is relaunched.

Simplest fix I can see would be to just drop the `SuccessfulExit` key from the KeepAlive dict in `SQRLShipItLauncher.m`. ShipIt is a one-shot installer and the "relaunch on unsuccessful exit" semantics aren't really doing anything useful in practice — if the bundle copy fails, re-running ShipIt isn't going to fix the filesystem state, and the cost of keeping it is a latent deadlock on newer macOS. Would slot in as a new patch alongside the existing `patches/squirrel.mac/` set. Alternatively kickstart the job explicitly after `SMJobSubmit` returns, which is what #197 was doing in 2017 — functionally works but feels like treating the symptom rather than the cause.

Workaround for any users hitting this in the meantime:

    launchctl enable   gui/$(id -u)/<app-bundle-id>.ShipIt
    launchctl kickstart -p gui/$(id -u)/<app-bundle-id>.ShipIt

### Electron Version

37.6.0 (bundled in Discord 0.0.383 — see Additional Information for why I'm filing downstream)

### What operating system(s) are you using?

macOS

### Operating System Version

Darwin 25.3.0

### What arch are you using?

arm64 (including Apple Silicon)

### Last Known Working Electron version

Unknown. Prior updates on the same machine completed successfully through 2026-03-10 per `ShipIt_stderr.log`; the failure is latent and only surfaces once the ShipIt LaunchAgent gets `launchctl disable`d at some point and is then recovered.

### Expected Behavior

After `autoUpdater.quitAndInstall()`, the main process exits, ShipIt runs, the staged update is installed, and the app relaunches.

### Actual Behavior

Main process exits cleanly. ShipIt never spawns. `ShipIt_stderr.log` receives zero new lines across multiple update attempts. No error surfaced to the app, the user, or the unified log. Manual `launchctl kickstart` is the only recovery.

### Testcase Gist URL

_No response_

### Additional Information

Hit this chasing a Discord update that silently refused to apply. Discord ships Electron 37.6.0, so filing here rather than in Discord's support portal where it'll just get "please reinstall"ed — and reinstalling provably doesn't fix it because the bad state lives in launchd, not in the `.app` bundle.

Same bug as Squirrel/Squirrel.Mac#196 (filed 2017, still open, zero replies in 9 years) with an almost-fix in Squirrel/Squirrel.Mac#197 (closed unmerged). I left the full writeup with the actual launchctl state dump on the #196 thread, linking here for anyone who wants to skip ahead: https://github.com/Squirrel/Squirrel.Mac/issues/196#issuecomment-4219698997

Short version: after `SMJobSubmit` the ShipIt job is registered fine and `RunAtLoad` is set, but launchd pends the initial spawn on an unsatisfiable `successful exit` semaphore and the job never executes. `launchctl print gui/$(id -u)/com.hnc.Discord.ShipIt`:

    runs = 0
    pended nondemand spawn = semaphore
    semaphores = {
        successful exit => 0
    }

I think what's happening is that the `KeepAlive = { SuccessfulExit = NO; }` clause in `Squirrel/SQRLShipItLauncher.m` is being evaluated by launchd as a precondition for the *initial* spawn, not just for keepalive restarts. On older macOS the keepalive dict only kicked in after `runs >= 1`, so `RunAtLoad` always fired cleanly. On Darwin 25 (possibly earlier, haven't bisected) launchd is checking the clause before the first spawn, and since "previous run exited non-successfully" can never be true when `runs = 0`, the spawn pends indefinitely. `launchctl kickstart` bypasses the semaphore and ShipIt runs to completion immediately, which tells me the job itself is fine — it's the spawn gating that's broken.

There's a secondary condition needed for this to manifest organically: the affected user's `com.hnc.Discord.ShipIt`, `com.microsoft.VSCode.ShipIt`, and `com.anthropic.claudefordesktop.ShipIt` were all in the launchd disabled override list (`launchctl print-disabled gui/$(id -u)` reported `=> disabled` for all three). User has no memory of running `launchctl disable` — some hardening/privacy tool presumably did. Clearing the override with `launchctl enable` is necessary but not sufficient; the pended-semaphore state still blocks the first spawn after re-enable, and that's the half I think is actually a Squirrel/Electron concern, since it silently wedges any affected user permanently and there's nothing in the autoUpdater API that surfaces it.

This can be reproduced on any Electron app using `autoUpdater` without waiting for an organic disable — just induce the state manually:

    # pick any Electron app using autoUpdater
    launchctl disable gui/$(id -u)/<app-bundle-id>.ShipIt
    # trigger an update inside the app so SMJobSubmit gets called
    # (the update will silently fail to apply)
    launchctl enable gui/$(id -u)/<app-bundle-id>.ShipIt
    # inspect the submitted job
    launchctl print gui/$(id -u)/<app-bundle-id>.ShipIt

`runs = 0` and `pended nondemand spawn = semaphore` should both be visible, and the job will never spawn on its own from that state no matter how long you wait or how many times the app is relaunched.

Simplest fix I can see would be to just drop the `SuccessfulExit` key from the KeepAlive dict in `SQRLShipItLauncher.m`. ShipIt is a one-shot installer and the "relaunch on unsuccessful exit" semantics aren't really doing anything useful in practice — if the bundle copy fails, re-running ShipIt isn't going to fix the filesystem state, and the cost of keeping it is a latent deadlock on newer macOS. Would slot in as a new patch alongside the existing `patches/squirrel.mac/` set. Alternatively kickstart the job explicitly after `SMJobSubmit` returns, which is what #197 was doing in 2017 — functionally works but feels like treating the symptom rather than the cause.

Workaround for any users hitting this in the meantime:

    launchctl enable   gui/$(id -u)/<app-bundle-id>.ShipIt
    launchctl kickstart -p gui/$(id -u)/<app-bundle-id>.ShipIt

- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Electron Version

41.x.y

### What operating system(s) are you using?

macOS

### Operating System Version

Sequoia 15.7.4

### What arch are you using?

arm64 (including Apple Silicon)

### Last Known Working Electron version

_No response_

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

No

### Expected Behavior

I would expect that the type of the `options` passed to the `WindowOpenHandlerResponse.createWindow` function would include the `webContents` property. This property is set when `window.open` is called within a webview – and subsequently – the `setWindowOpenHandler` handler is called, which then returns a `createWindow` handler.

### Actual Behavior

The `webContents` property on the `BrowserWindowConstructorOptions` is not parts of the electron types.

### Testcase Gist URL

_No response_

### Additional Information

When you set a handler using `webContentsView.webContents.setWindowOpenHandler` and the handler is called (e.g. `window.open` is called by a website), you can return:

```
{
  action: 'allow',
  createWindow(options: BrowserWindowConstructorOptions) => {...},
}
```

The `options` that are passed `createWindow` will contain a `webContents` property that is not documented in the types.
We found out because if you return a different `WebContents` from the `createWindow` function, a specific error will be thrown and the Electron process will exit.

### Last Known Working Electron version

I don't know how to test

### Expected Behavior

After using `setSimpleFullScreen` to set with full screen, when display mp4 and enter fullscreen, 
1. mp4 can quit fullscreen after manually quit fullscreen
2. electron should keep fullscreen when set mp4 as fullscreen mode.

### Actual Behavior

**Problem Description**

On macOS with Electron, when using `setSimpleFullScreen`, playing an MP4 video on a page and clicking the video player’s fullscreen button causes Electron to exit SimpleFullScreen mode. After this, the MP4 video cannot exit fullscreen.

This issue also occurs when the page loads third-party content via an <iframe>. If the iframe triggers fullscreen playback using requestFullscreen, the problem will appear as well.

Testing shows that using `setFullScreen` (regular fullscreen) does not trigger this issue. However, due to specific business requirements, we must use `setSimpleFullScreen`.

Note: The issue is not limited to MP4 videos; any event that triggers `requestFullscreen` can potentially cause this behavior.

https://gist.github.com/chinaofmelon/aa7e3f334507df9c4936e1d41d72c3e1

nodes.title: EXC_BREAKPOINT / pointer authentication trap in CFRetain during async OSR paint handler (macOS arm64, 41.1.1)
nodes.body:
## Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success.

## Electron Version

41.1.1

## What operating system(s) are you using?

macOS

## Operating System Version

macOS 26.4 (build 25E246) — Darwin 25.4.0, ARM64 (native, not translated)

## What arch are you using?

arm64 (Apple Silicon — MacBookPro18,3)

## Last Known Working Electron Version

Unknown — first observed on 41.x

## Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

No

---

## Expected Behavior

An app using offscreen rendering (`offscreen: { useSharedTexture: true }`) with an async paint handler runs stably. Specifically, calling `sharedTexture.importSharedTexture()` from within a microtask (Promise callback) that originates in the `paint` event handler should not crash.

## Actual Behavior

The app crashes with `EXC_BREAKPOINT (SIGTRAP)` on the main thread (CrBrowserMain). The ESR register contains `pointer authentication trap DA` — an ARM64 PAC authentication failure occurring inside `CFRetain` in CoreFoundation. The crash happens during Node.js microtask queue processing while a native JS object wrapper is being constructed via `v8::Function::NewInstanceWithSideEffectType`.

The crash is reproducible on the same machine across multiple sessions. It is triggered by window resize or DevTools open/close, but also occurs spontaneously after a period of operation.

## Code Pattern

```js
// webPreferences: { offscreen: { useSharedTexture: true } }

const { sharedTexture } = require('electron')

win.webContents.on('paint', (details) => {
  const texture = details.texture
  if (!texture) return

  // Async IIFE — native texture objects accessed across microtask boundary
  void (async () => {
    try {
      const result = await publishAsync({ texture })
    } finally {
      texture.release?.()
    }
  })()
})

async function publishAsync({ texture }) {
  // importSharedTexture creates a native JS wrapper via NewInstanceWithSideEffectType.
  // CFRetain on the underlying ObjC pointer then fails with a PAC trap.
  const imported = sharedTexture.importSharedTexture({
    textureInfo: texture.textureInfo,
    allReferencesReleased() {},
  })
  imported?.release?.()
}
```

## Crash Details

**Exception:** `EXC_BREAKPOINT (SIGTRAP)`  
**ESR:** `0xf200c472` — `(Breakpoint) pointer authentication trap DA`  
**FAR:** `0x0`  
**PC:** `0x18b497148` (CoreFoundation `CFRetain + 84`)

**Triggered thread stack trace (CrBrowserMain):**

```
CoreFoundation             CFRetain + 84
Electron Framework         node::PrincipalRealm::tick_callback_function() const + 249520
Electron Framework         node::PrincipalRealm::tick_callback_function() const + 263000
Electron Framework         node::PrincipalRealm::tick_callback_function() const + 262748
Electron Framework         node::PrincipalRealm::tick_callback_function() const + 262376
?                          <jit> (x8 unresolved JIT frames)
Electron Framework         v8::Function::NewInstanceWithSideEffectType(...) + 2204
Electron Framework         v8::Isolate::SuppressMicrotaskExecutionScope::...() + 228
Electron Framework         v8::Isolate::SuppressMicrotaskExecutionScope::...() + 132
Electron Framework         cppgc::subtle::NoGarbageCollectionScope::Leave(...) + 432
Electron Framework         node::InternalCallbackScope::Close() + 360
Electron Framework         node::CallbackScope::~CallbackScope() + 56
Electron Framework         node::PrincipalRealm::tick_callback_function() const + 416400
... (V8 internals / run loop)
CoreFoundation             __CFRUNLOOP_IS_CALLING_OUT_TO_A_SOURCE0_PERFORM_FUNCTION__ + 28
CoreFoundation             __CFRunLoopRun + 820
AppKit                     -[NSApplication run] + 368
Electron Framework         ElectronMain + 120
dyld                       start + 6992
```

## Analysis

The crash path is:

1. AppKit RunLoop fires a CF source0 callback
2. Node.js processes its microtask queue (`tick_callback_function`)
3. JIT-compiled JS calls `NewInstanceWithSideEffectType` — constructing a native Electron object wrapper
4. Electron calls `CFRetain` on the underlying ObjC pointer
5. ARM64 PAC authenticates the pointer → **authentication failure** → `EXC_BREAKPOINT`

The PAC trap (`pointer authentication trap DA`) means `CFRetain` received a pointer whose signature doesn't match the current process context — consistent with an ObjC object pointer that originated in a different process (e.g. the GPU/renderer process) being retained in the browser process during native wrapper construction.

No native addons appear in the crash thread frames — this is entirely within Electron's own code path.

Related: #50247 (different trigger, same platform/exception type)

Windows ### Operating System Version Windows 11 25H2 ### What arch are you using? x64 ### Last Known Working Electron version _No response_ ### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome? No ### Expected Behavior An 800x600 window with `frame: true` should measure 800x600 including the titlebar. ### Actual Behavior The window measures 784x592, even though `getBounds()` and other APIs report 800x600. You can measure with the screenshot tool (assuming 100% scaling) or simply by creating a window with a frame and dragging it on top of one without. ### Testcase Gist URL https://gist.github.com/f663c54e89ca040de882ca00dabbc701 ### Additional Information The shrinking happens because `getBounds()` and `setBounds()` operate directly on the invisible widget (HWND). The visible part of the window gets shrunk down by Chromium to fit resize insets (8px on each side and bottom, so width-16px, height-8px). As a result, windows end up smaller and with less usable space than they are supposed to have. This isn't an issue in Chromium where developers do not have direct control over window dimensions, but it is in Electron. Even if you account for the space that's intentionally taken up by the titlebar/menubar when `useContentSize: false`, the content area ends up too small: it should be ~800x543, not 784x535. (This is not a case of the "window frame" taking up the space, which would be understandable. These insets are only present to support resize hit targets.) This problem was recently addressed on Linux (https://github.com/electron/electron/pull/49209) and can be solved the same way on Windows. https://github.com/electron/electron/pull/50706 addresses it for frameless windows with external resize targets.

Tahoe 26.3

### What arch are you using?

### Last Known Working Electron version

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

Yes

### Expected Behavior

App launches successfully in MAS / TestFlight sandbox on ARM64, as it does when distributed as a notarised DMG.

### Actual Behavior

App crashes instantly on launch with EXC_BREAKPOINT (SIGTRAP) on Thread 22 (ThreadPoolSingleThreadForegroundBlocking0). Symbolicated stack terminates at v8::internal::ThreadIsolation::UnregisterWasmAllocation. Crash occurs only under MAS/TestFlight sandbox entitlements on ARM64. The same build runs correctly as a notarised DMG and on Intel.

### Testcase Gist URL

_No response_

### Additional Information

This crash is confirmed and tracked upstream in Chromium issue 499332110 (P2/S2, assigned to vahl@chromium.org, "Unconfirmed" label removed 2026-04-06): https://issues.chromium.org/issues/499332110

Root cause: ThreadIsolation::UnregisterWasmAllocation calls mprotect() on MAP_JIT-allocated pages. macOS 26 App Sandbox tightens enforcement — MAP_JIT pages require pthread_jit_write_protect_np() for permission changes. Apple DTS (Quinn "The Eskimo!") has confirmed this is a V8 API conformance problem, not an Apple bug. Reference: "Porting just-in-time compilers to Apple Silicon" (developer.apple.com).

Same progression as macOS 11.2 / nodejs/node#37276. This crash currently blocks MAS submission for sandboxed Electron apps on macOS 26 ARM64.

Request: please subscribe to Chromium 499332110 and ensure the V8 fix lands in Electron's next V8 upgrade.
